main_issue: Whether the shared house fund should pay for the alcohol bought for the housewarming, and then how to plan food for guests.

A-B.evidence: B endorsed A's offer to cover alcohol personally (turn 8: 'that sounds fair'); they then agreed on the food plan (turns 17-18).

A-C.evidence: C objected to using the fund for alcohol (turns 3, 5); A moved to cover the alcohol himself (turn 7); C accepted: 'Okay, that works. Thanks, Agent A' (turn 9).

A-D.evidence: D said they don't drink either (turn 6); A conceded and offered to pay for alcohol (turn 7); D agreed to the food plan (turns 16-17) and did not object.

B-C.evidence: B said the plan is fair (turn 8), C accepted it (turn 9); B suggested halal food and C agreed (turns 11, 13, 14).

B-D.evidence: B raised the no-beef need for D's side (turn 11); D added Indian food (turn 16) and B said 'Okay, good' (turn 18).

C-D.evidence: Both objected to the fund paying for alcohol since they don't drink (turns 3, 5, 6); both accepted the final plans without conflict.
